title: How Nude Beaches Work
summary: Josh and Chuck open with Josh's tooth extraction story from a Isle of Palms, South Carolina vacation, then turn to nude beaches. They discuss personal experiences with clothing-optional beaches (Canaveral National Seashore's Klondike Beach, Wreck Beach in Vancouver), the difference between naturist resorts and public clothing-optional beaches, nudity attitudes in Europe and Australia based on a 2016 survey, Hollywood Beach in Miami, Haulover Park, Black's Beach in San Diego, Cape Cod National Seashore's nudity ban, Milwaukee's Paradise Beach, Victorian bathing cabanas, etiquette tips for nude beaches, and listener mail about a medical school interview.
topics: Cape Cod National Seashore nudity ban

segments.title: Tooth extraction story and nude beach lead-in
segments.summary: Josh describes losing a tooth and getting it extracted at an oral surgeon in Mount Pleasant during a South Carolina vacation, with local seafood and dental anecdotes. The hosts then segue to whether Josh went to a nude beach, mentioning the Isle of Palms tradition of swimming in tuxedo pants to cover up from sea turtles.

segments.title: Personal experiences at nude beaches
segments.summary: Josh recounts visiting Klondike Beach at Canaveral National Seashore in Florida, where he saw a clothing-optional beach with few nude people. Chuck describes a trip with a friend where they camped on Klondike Beach and a naked older man struck up a conversation. They discuss Wreck Beach in Vancouver, which has a reputation as a permissive beach that has been cracked down on recently.

segments.title: Naturism vs. public clothing-optional beaches
segments.summary: The hosts distinguish naturist resorts, which require nudity and membership, from public clothing-optional beaches where nudity is optional. They note that public nude beaches often lose control when outside elements bring partying and public sex, prompting complaints and government intervention. They also discuss personal experiences with topless beaches in Europe.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: The hosts take a break from the episode.

segments.title: Nude beach attitudes in Europe, Australia, and the US
segments.summary: The hosts cite a 2016 survey of about ninety countries on attitudes toward public nude sunbathing. Austria and Germany ranked highly, with Italians least accepting. The hosts discuss Australia's changing relationship with nude beaches and the early nude beach in Bordeaux, France, and nude footage from Georgia in the 1920s.

segments.title: Air Force Beach and Hollywood Beach Miami
segments.summary: The hosts describe Air Force Beach, a private island near Palm Beach owned by John D. MacArthur, where one side became a popular nude area until the county took over after his death. They also discuss Haulover Park in Miami, described as one of the largest nude beaches in the United States, and its party atmosphere.

segments.title: Cape Cod nudity ban, Milwaukee, and Black's Beach
segments.summary: The hosts explain that Cape Cod National Seashore banned public nudity in the 1970s after a dispute, and the ban was upheld in court, making it reportedly the only national park with a specific nudity ban. They discuss how nude beaches typically start as remote unofficial spots and are later legislated after complaints. They mention Paradise Beach in Milwaukee, which closed after sex and drinking spread there, and Black's Beach in San Diego.

segments.title: Nude beach etiquette and safety tips
segments.summary: The hosts discuss rules for nude beaches: no sex, don't be a creep, avoid photographing people, don't sit right next to others, bring towels to sit on and dry off with, and sunscreen. They also discuss the Victorian-era horse-drawn bathing cabanas in Australia and England and Brighton's first official nude beach.

segments.title: Listener mail: medical school interview
segments.summary: A listener named Isaac Lamb writes that a shared love of the show with an interviewer helped him get into medical school. The hosts congratulate him and mention the ways to contact the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and provide contact information for social media and email.
